clue.text: Please Ray with gift that's unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of ray and gift are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win Ray over with a present out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's unusual' rearranges RAY and GIFT together; 'Please' is a verb here, not a polite request.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify someone is to give them satisfaction, a direct synonym of the verb please.

clue.text: He leaves his country to be protected by another

definitions.text: He leaves his country to be protected by another

parts.words: He leaves his country to be protected by another
parts.note: a straightforward description of someone fleeing their homeland to find asylum elsewhere

explanation.surface: A man flees his homeland seeking another nation's protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flees their homeland and seeks asylum abroad is the very picture of a displaced person.

clue.text: I go round Italian city

indicators.note: the word for go is placed round the letter I

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn

explanation.surface: A tourist travels round an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' reads as a phrase, but 'go' gives TURN and 'round' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, Torino in Italian, is the capital of Piedmont in northern Italy.

clue.text: Charge soldiers found in brawl

indicators.note: the soldiers are discovered inside the brawl

parts.note: a brawl is a fight
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops are accused after being caught in a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation, but here it is a fee paid for transporting goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight can mean the fee for carrying goods, so a transport charge.

clue.text: Missionary who can handle a spoon?

definitions.text: Missionary who can handle a spoon?

parts.words: Missionary who can handle a spoon?
parts.note: ... spoons are silver spoons whose handles end in a figure of one of Christ's twelve missionaries

explanation.surface: A preacher on a mission is asked whether he is any good with cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: The handle is literal: the figure forms the end of the spoon's handle, not a person holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve disciples were sent out to preach, the first missionaries of the faith.

clue.text: Quietly share out a few words from tourist guide?

definitions.text: a few words from tourist guide?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: out signals the letters of share are put out of order

explanation.surface: A tour guide softly hands round a few useful expressions.
explanation.walkthrough: A phrase book is the tourist guide that gives a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a small group of words, the kind collected in a phrasebook for travellers.

clue.text: Shoulders no responsibility?

parts.note: a shrug of the shoulders is the gesture of dismissing a matter as no concern of one's own

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take on any burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something lightly as unimportant, often with a lift of the shoulders.

clue.text: It makes no difference to these girls should I depart

definitions.text: It makes no difference to these girls should I depart

parts.words: It makes no difference to these girls should I depart
parts.note: take away the letter I from the word for these girls and what remains still means girls

explanation.surface: Some young women are quite indifferent to whether the speaker leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I and LASSES remains: girls either way, so it makes no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassies is a Scottish and northern word for girls or young women.

clue.text: Four on the fiddle?

parts.note: on the fiddle suggests a swindle, but here four players are on bowed instruments

explanation.surface: Four people are running a dishonest scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' is British slang for cheating; here it means playing violins and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber group of two violins, viola and cello, so four musicians playing stringed instruments.

clue.text: A return of service which is some way off

indicators.note: a return here is a turning back, so the word for the service is read from its end to its start

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis player's returned serve lands far from the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of service' sounds like tennis, but the service here is one of the armed forces, the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated a long distance away is said to lie at a distance, far off.

clue.text: Gain admission by force and initiative

parts.note: to gain admission to a place is to go in
to prise something is to force it open with leverage

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks into a building by force and shows some initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise as a quality means boldness and readiness to undertake new projects, i.e. initiative.

clue.text: Drink triple gin, initially, with one rum

indicators.note: rum in its old sense means odd or strange, so the letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: the first letter of gin taken three times

explanation.surface: A drinker orders three gins and a rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like another drink but is the adjective meaning odd, shuffling GGG with ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a beverage of eggs, milk and sugar, often spiked with spirits, so a drink.

clue.text: Status symbols?

parts.note: badges and emblems worn to show rank or office literally symbolise a person's status

explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are the badges or marks of rank and office, which literally show one's standing.

clue.text: All set to accept redundancy

definitions.meaning: willing to leave one's job when posts are cut

explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared to depart means both fully prepared and willing to leave a post being cut.

clue.text: Line up on quarterdeck in formal wear

parts.note: to dress ranks is the military order to line up
read as quarter deck: a suit is one quarter of a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Sailors parade on the ship's quarterdeck in their finest uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The quarterdeck is a ship's officers' deck, but split it reads quarter (of a) deck: one of four card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress suit is a man's formal evening outfit, so clothing for formal occasions.

clue.text: Give a lift to one in the army

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the word for the army

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier is given a ride somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise something up, especially by ropes or tackle, so to give it a lift.

clue.text: Be sent back to bunk, having weakened

indicators.note: something sent back is returned the way it came, so the two letters of be are read in reverse

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly is told to go back to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: When a tide or strength ebbs it recedes or declines, so it has lessened or faded.

clue.text: Some reservation about giving a player a yellow card?

definitions.meaning: an arrangement made in advance for a seat, room or table

definitions.text: giving a player a yellow card?
definitions.meaning: a referee notes a cautioned player's name in his notebook

explanation.surface: A referee has doubts before cautioning a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking is both an advance reservation and a referee's caution recorded against a player.

clue.text: A survivor in the heat

parts.note: in sport a heat is a preliminary round, and someone who survives it goes through to the next stage

explanation.surface: Someone endures a blazing hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' suggests high temperature, but it is a preliminary race.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who gets through a qualifying round to the next stage of a contest.

clue.text: Wash the one French article that's German

parts.note: in French the is la and one is un
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: A laundry is run by a French woman and a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' applies to both 'the' and 'one' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash and iron them.

clue.text: Rising unit of temperature — about a thousand — appeared

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from bottom to top
the unit of temperature is placed around the letter for a thousand

parts.note: a degree is a unit of temperature
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A rise in temperature of a thousand degrees showed itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DEGREE round M to make DEGREME, which 'Rising' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, so emerged means came into sight or appeared.

clue.text: Notice opening time before Christmas

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: A notice announces a shop opening just before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the church season of the four weeks leading up to Christmas.

clue.text: Regard as deliberate

definitions.meaning: to look upon or think of in a particular way
the verb, to think over carefully

explanation.definitionFit: Consider means both to regard someone as something and to think carefully, to ponder.

clue.text: Loan shark certain to be found in the city

indicators.note: the word for certain is placed inside the word for the city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's favourite city
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A predatory moneylender is bound to be working in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' tempts towards London's financial City, apt for a moneylender, but it is the ancient city of Ur.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, exactly what a loan shark does.

clue.text: City game to lift boycott

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word raises it, so its letters read upwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to boycott is to ban

explanation.surface: A city's authorities agree to end a sporting boycott.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift boycott' suggests ending a ban; 'to lift' reverses RU, and 'boycott' is BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means of or relating to a city or town.

clue.text: Nominal chief of the maths department?

definitions.text: Nominal chief of the maths department?

parts.words: Nominal chief of the maths department?
parts.note: a leader in name only, playfully pictured as the head of those who deal in figures

explanation.surface: A school's mathematics chief holds the title but no real power.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead is a leader in name only, with no real authority; the head of figures is the joke.

clue.text: Lots of trousers

definitions.meaning: ... of something means plenty of it
Oxford ... are wide-legged trousers, so ... can mean trousers

explanation.definitionFit: Bags is informal for plenty, and a British name for loose, wide trousers.

clue.text: Stir it in a football crowd

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators attending a match

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to whip up a football crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A football gate is the attendance at a match, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or shake, whether a liquid or people.

clue.text: Uncertain range of French explosive projectile

indicators.note: uncertain letters are not fixed in place, so the word range is rearranged

parts.note: de is the French word for of

explanation.surface: A French missile is fired with doubtful accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand or launched, an explosive missile.
